passages.text: Then the LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you may bring as your offering an animal from the herd or the flock.
passages.sermon:
The LORD called to Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses from the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD said these words to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD told Moses to say this to them.
If any person among you brings an offering to the LORD, do this.
You may bring your offering from the animals.
You may bring your offering from the herd.
You may bring your offering from the flock.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֖א אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו מֵאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי־ יַקְרִ֥יב מִכֶּ֛ם קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה מִן־ הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה מִן־ הַבָּקָר֙ וּמִן־ הַצֹּ֔אן תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ אֶת־ קָרְבַּנְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: If one’s offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to present an unblemished male. He must bring it to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for its acceptance before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions to Moses for the Israelites.
God told Moses about offerings.
A person may want to give a burnt offering to God.
The person must choose an animal from the herd.
The animal must be a male.
The animal must have no blemish or defect.
The person must bring the animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The person brings the animal so that God will accept the offering.
passages.original: אִם־ עֹלָ֤ה קָרְבָּנוֹ֙ מִן־ הַבָּקָ֔ר זָכָ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יַקְרִיבֶ֑נּוּ אֶל־ פֶּ֝תַח אֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ יַקְרִ֣יב אֹת֔וֹ לִרְצֹנ֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
passages.sermon:
The man brings a burnt offering to God.
He places his hand on the head of the animal.
God accepts the offering for the man.
The offering makes atonement for the man.
passages.original: וְסָמַ֣ךְ יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הָעֹלָ֑ה וְנִרְצָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: And he shall slaughter the young bull before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to present the blood and sprinkle it on all sides of the altar at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
A man brings a young bull as a burnt offering.
He must slaughter the young bull before the LORD.
Aaron’s sons serve as priests.
The priests take the blood from the bull.
The priests sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar.
The altar stands at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת־ בֶּ֥ן הַבָּקָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠הִקְרִיבוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֤ן הַֽכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֶת־ הַדָּ֔ם וְזָרְק֨וּ אֶת־ הַדָּ֤ם עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב אֲשֶׁר־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: Next, he is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
passages.sermon: The man brings a burnt offering to the altar.\r\nHe must skin the burnt offering.\r\nHe must cut the burnt offering into pieces.
passages.original: וְהִפְשִׁ֖יט אֶת־ הָעֹלָ֑ה וְנִתַּ֥ח אֹתָ֖הּ לִנְתָחֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: The sons of Aaron the priest shall put a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
passages.sermon: The sons of Aaron are priests.\r\nThe sons of Aaron must put fire on the altar.\r\nThe sons of Aaron must arrange wood on the fire.
passages.original: וְ֠נָתְנוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֧ן הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֵ֖שׁ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְעָרְכ֥וּ עֵצִ֖ים עַל־ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Then Aaron’s sons the priests are to arrange the pieces, including the head and the fat, atop the burning wood on the altar.
passages.sermon:
Aaron’s sons are priests.
They take the pieces of the offering.
They include the head and the fat.
They place these pieces on the wood.
The wood is on the fire.
The fire is on the altar.
passages.original: וְעָרְכ֗וּ בְּנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אֵ֚ת הַנְּתָחִ֔ים אֶת־ הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְאֶת־ הַפָּ֑דֶר עַל־ הָעֵצִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall burn all of it on the altar as a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The priest must wash the entrails with water.
The priest must wash the legs with water.
The priest must burn all of the animal on the altar.
This is a burnt offering.
This offering is made by fire.
This offering gives a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: וְקִרְבּ֥וֹ וּכְרָעָ֖יו יִרְחַ֣ץ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְהִקְטִ֨יר הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־ הַכֹּל֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עֹלָ֛ה אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־ נִיח֖וֹחַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: If, however, one’s offering is a burnt offering from the flock—from the sheep or goats—he is to present an unblemished male.
passages.sermon:
A person may bring an offering to God.
The offering may be a burnt offering.
The offering may come from the flock.
The flock may include sheep or goats.
The person must choose a male animal.
The animal must have no blemish.
The person must present this unblemished male as the offering.
passages.original: וְאִם־ מִן־ הַצֹּ֨אן קָרְבָּנ֧וֹ מִן־ הַכְּשָׂבִ֛ים א֥וֹ מִן־ הָעִזִּ֖ים לְעֹלָ֑ה זָכָ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יַקְרִיבֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron’s sons the priests are to sprinkle its blood against the altar on all sides.
passages.sermon:
A man brings an animal for a burnt offering to the LORD.
He must kill the animal.
He must do this on the north side of the altar.
He does this before the LORD.
Aaron’s sons are priests.
The priests take the animal’s blood.
The priests sprinkle the blood on all sides of the altar.
passages.original: וְשָׁחַ֨ט אֹת֜וֹ עַ֣ל יֶ֧רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ צָפֹ֖נָה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְזָרְק֡וּ בְּנֵי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים אֶת־ דָּמ֛וֹ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

passages.text: He is to cut the animal into pieces, and the priest shall arrange them, including the head and fat, atop the burning wood that is on the altar.
passages.sermon:
The man brings an animal for a burnt offering.
The animal comes from the flock.
The man must cut the animal into pieces.
He must also separate the head and the fat.
The priest takes the pieces.
The priest takes the head and the fat.
The priest arranges all these parts on the wood.
The wood is on the fire.
The fire is on the altar.
passages.original: וְנִתַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִנְתָחָ֔יו וְאֶת־ רֹאשׁ֖וֹ וְאֶת־ פִּדְר֑וֹ וְעָרַ֤ךְ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹתָ֔ם עַל־ הָֽעֵצִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: The entrails and legs must be washed with water, and the priest shall bring all of it and burn it on the altar; it is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The entrails and the legs must be washed with water.
The priest must take all the parts of the animal.
The priest must burn all the parts on the altar.
This is a burnt offering.
This offering is made by fire.
This offering is a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: וְהַקֶּ֥רֶב וְהַכְּרָעַ֖יִם יִרְחַ֣ץ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְהִקְרִ֨יב הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־ הַכֹּל֙ וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עֹלָ֣ה ה֗וּא אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: If, instead, one’s offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to present a turtledove or a young pigeon.
passages.sermon:
A person may want to give an offering to the LORD.
This offering may be a burnt offering.
The offering may be from birds.
The person must bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.
He must present this bird as his offering.
passages.original: וְאִ֧ם מִן־ הָע֛וֹף עֹלָ֥ה קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהִקְרִ֣יב מִן־ הַתֹּרִ֗ים א֛וֹ מִן־ בְּנֵ֥י הַיּוֹנָ֖ה אֶת־ קָרְבָּנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the priest shall bring it to the altar, twist off its head, and burn it on the altar; its blood should be drained out on the side of the altar.
passages.sermon:
The priest takes the bird.
The priest brings the bird to the altar.
The priest twists off the bird’s head.
The priest burns the bird on the altar.
The priest drains the bird’s blood on the side of the altar.
passages.original: וְהִקְרִיב֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֶל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וּמָלַק֙ אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְהִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְנִמְצָ֣ה דָמ֔וֹ עַ֖ל קִ֥יר הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

passages.text: And he is to remove the crop with its contents and throw it to the east side of the altar, in the place for ashes.
passages.sermon:
The priest must remove the bird’s crop with its contents.
He must take the crop and its contents away from the bird.
He must throw the crop and its contents on the east side of the altar.
He must place it in the area where the ashes are kept.
passages.original: וְהֵסִ֥יר אֶת־ מֻרְאָת֖וֹ בְּנֹצָתָ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלִ֨יךְ אֹתָ֜הּ אֵ֤צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ קֵ֔דְמָה אֶל־ מְק֖וֹם הַדָּֽשֶׁן׃

passages.text: He shall tear it open by its wings, without dividing the bird completely. And the priest is to burn it on the altar atop the burning wood. It is a burnt offering, an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A priest serves at the altar of the LORD.
The priest takes the bird for the burnt offering.
He tears the bird open by its wings.
He does not separate the bird into two parts.
The priest burns the bird on the altar.
He places it on the wood that is on the fire.
This is a burnt offering.
The fire consumes the offering.
The offering gives a pleasing smell to the LORD.
passages.original: וְשִׁסַּ֨ע אֹת֣וֹ בִכְנָפָיו֮ לֹ֣א יַבְדִּיל֒ וְהִקְטִ֨יר אֹת֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עַל־ הָעֵצִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הָאֵ֑שׁ עֹלָ֣ה ה֗וּא אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃ס
